patterns.what_worked: Reading the t2 port map end to end before opening an editor, then re-verifying the three load-bearing API claims against origin/forever (Blizzard_AuraContainer load flags + securecopy sort enums, AddAuraGroup securecopy/validation, secretwrap container sizing) removed the two traps the report warned about: the load-time gate is safe because the addon is not LoadOnDemand, and the fixed-band anchor is required because container geometry can be secret. Writing the suite first (red on the missing module) made every API decision testable before it existed, and the 12-mutation run proved the checks are not vacuous - it also caught a real fixture weakness (a table-shaped 'secret' made a type guard look like a secret guard) which is now a numeric secret sentinel.
patterns.what_was_hard: The biggest judgement call was combat: the brief says native creation must never happen in lockdown, but without a class-file hook the module had no retry path. Creating only the plain driver Frame during lockdown (never an AuraContainer) and documenting/testing that split was the honest resolution. Second: the duration text above debuff icons needs vertical clearance, so the reserved band is size + 16 px (the reference's DEBUFF_TEXT_CLEARANCE), not just the icon height - an easy off-by-a-band in a layout that can never be measured.
patterns.skill_gap: No offline way to prove taint behaviour of SetPoint/Show on a container with the UntrustedLayoutScriptExecution aspect, or that tainted creation of the template works: those stay UNCONFIRMED with exact /run probes. Also the option-table widget set could only be exercised by loading option_tables.lua in a sandbox (the real AceConfig render is untested offline).
